plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers with many layered petals. It thrives in partial shade and acidic, well-drained soil, and is a staple of winter gardens in mild climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (December to April in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and eastern China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Western Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, produces all true tea. Camellia japonica was the inspiration for many Japanese poems and is the official flower of several Japanese prefectures.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant blossoms on bare branches in the cold of late winter, before its leaves appear. It is deeply admired in East Asian culture as a symbol of perseverance and hope.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: Native to southern China; cultivated across Japan, Korea, and Taiwan, with plum blossom festivals held in Japanese gardens
plants.funFact: In China, the plum blossom is one of the 'Three Friends of Winter' along with pine and bamboo, and it is the national flower of Taiwan.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with drooping, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It often pushes up through snow and forms large drifts in woodlands and gardens.
plants.location: Native to Europe from the Pyrenees to Ukraine; naturalized in the UK and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops contain galantamine, a compound used in medications to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease. Enthusiasts called 'galanthophiles' pay high prices for rare cultivars.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Not typically blooming in February in most places, so this entry instead highlights the Southern Hemisphere summer flowering of a related showy plant: Agapanthus praecox, a clump-forming perennial with large rounded clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers on tall stalks above strap-like leaves.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (December to March)
plants.location: Native to South Africa; widely planted in Australia, New Zealand, and coastal California
plants.funFact: Agapanthus means 'flower of love' in Greek, from agape (love) and anthos (flower), which makes it a fitting February 14 bloom.
